summary.headline: Ador Welding Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 23% YoY to INR345 crores, but gross margin fell to 34.2% on steel-led input inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 23% YoY to INR345 crores and H1 revenue rose 23% to INR654 crores, supported by infrastructure, power, oil and gas, railways, shipbuilding, defence and heavy fabrication demand. Gross margin fell to 34.2% as steel and other raw material costs rose sharply; management attributed about 80% of the dip to input inflation and 15-20% to aggressive growth and product mix. EBITDA grew 9% in the quarter and H1 EBITDA margin was 11.2%, slightly above last year. Management said calibrated price increases were taken, with pass-through lagging in Q2 and improving in Q3, and declared an interim dividend of INR7.5 per share.

financial_highlights.change: H1 at upper end of range
from about INR0.27 crores at FY26

segments.name: Consumables
segments.commentary: Management said consumables tend to have strong returns, depending on product mix; specialised high-performance products are being introduced for demanding applications. No segment revenue figures were given.

segments.name: Industrial M&R (Fontech)
segments.commentary: Management said Fontech is around INR220-230 crores in revenue, roughly flat to pre-merger levels, and that fabrication-related products were moved into the wider welding business. Growth expected at 8-12%, well below other markets.

segments.name: Equipment and automation
segments.commentary: Hypertherm master distribution in India for plasma cutting, Liburdi Dimetrics orbital welding tie-up, and WelDoS welder-data add-on. Automation margins are expected to take time to reach equipment and consumables levels.

segments.name: Flare segment
segments.commentary: Management said the flare segment is essentially exited, with revenue insignificant and no EBITDA losses in H1.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 12-13%, to be pushed higher over time.
Gross margin ideally at least 36-38%, with recovery expected from Q3 FY27; management said early days in Q3.
Volume growth expected at high-single to double digits, with sales teams given aggressive H2 targets.
Aspiration of about INR2,000 crores revenue by FY29; management said the company is fairly on track.
Capex of about INR30-35 crores in FY27, with an elevated INR60-70 crores in FY27-28 before reverting to a normal INR35-40 crores a year; no debt or equity dilution planned.
capex_capacity: Normal annual capex is about INR35-40 crores, with FY27 at about INR30-35 crores.
FY27 and FY28 capex expected at INR60-70 crores, driven by investment in a new consumables line.
Management said the balance sheet is strong enough to fund the capex without debt or equity.
Five manufacturing units; management said investment is to modernise the base and support scaling.
demand_pricing: Steel prices rose about 7-8% QoQ in Q2 FY27 per management; other inputs such as copper, electronics/PCBs and imported components also rose, and freight added to import costs.
Price increases were taken in line with steel moves, with pass-through lagging due to timing and contracts; management said most is being passed through now.
Export mix: Middle East about 80-85% of exports (Dubai hub), plus the US, parts of Africa and two European markets with a third being entered.
Management said order book is confidential and declined to quantify it; shipbuilding opportunity described as significant.
Inventory and payables rose at 30 September: about 75-80% from order backlog and 15-20% from steel availability concerns.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin level and what drove the Q2 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 80% of the dip to input cost inflation and 15-20% to aggressive growth and product mix; sustainable EBITDA margin is 12-13%, with gross margin ideally 36-38%.

qa_highlights.question: What was the volume growth in Q2 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was about mid-teens in Q2; management expects it to continue, with aggressive targets for H2 and international markets offering upside.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR2,000 crore FY29 revenue target achievable and does the current capacity support it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is fairly on track. It expects 60-70% of incremental growth to come from product mix, one-third from innovations, partnerships and automation, and noted capex of INR60-70 crores in FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did short-term borrowing rise to about INR28 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly LCs and BGs, plus a smaller working-capital component and strategic steel purchases; management said H1 should not be read as a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Are there acquisition plans in automation or robotics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said options are being explored in automation, but it is very early and the ecosystem is small, so nothing is imminent.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company's share of wallet with large customers improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top 50 and top 100 customers are a focus area, with hiring and strategy in place, but this takes time; product gaps from the last 2-3 years have largely been plugged.

risks_watch: Steel and imported raw material inflation, with management unable to say when steel prices will soften.
Pass-through lag and contract timing; Q3 gross margin recovery is the key test.
Working capital: inventory build and payables decline, plus rising short-term borrowing (about INR28 crores).
Export concentration: Middle East about 80-85% of exports.
Inorganic growth and automation acquisitions remain at an early exploration stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and long-term targets, but openly cautious on Q2 margins, which management said were a larger dip than it is comfortable with. Management was evasive on steel price outlook, raw material breakup, order book and acquisition specifics.
key_quotes: It has to be between the 12%-13% level.
Our job is to get it to between that 12% to 13% level and then push upwards from there.
That will not be the norm.
I'm not stressed about will the market now readjust.

adds.what: New consumables line (capex INR60-70 crores over FY27-28, no capacity size stated)

growth.why: Management guides high-single to double-digit volume growth in H2 and an INR2,000 crore revenue aspiration by FY29 (said fairly on track), backed by mid-teens Q2 volume growth, price pass-through and an unquantified order book; the new consumables line (INR60-70 crore capex over FY27-28) has no stated capacity size or timing.
